paragraphs_en: The Prophet ﷺ said dreams are of three kinds:
1. A true, good dream: glad tidings from Allah
2. From Satan: a dream that brings grief
3. The self talking: what a person was thinking about during the day

title_en: True dreams are part of prophethood
paragraphs_en: The good dream of a righteous person is one of forty-six parts of prophethood.
The Prophet ﷺ said: nothing of prophethood remains except the glad tidings (mubashshirat), meaning good dreams.
Revelation to the Prophet ﷺ began with true dreams. Every dream he saw came true like the light of dawn.

title_en: Dreams of the prophets in the Quran
paragraphs_en: Prophet Yusuf (AS) saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him; years later the dream came true.
Prophet Ibrahim (AS) saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son, because the dreams of prophets are revelation.
The king of Egypt dreamed of seven fat cows and seven lean ones, and Prophet Yusuf (AS) interpreted it.
The Prophet ﷺ dreamed of entering al-Masjid al-Haram, and the dream came true.
1. Thank Allah (say Alhamdulillah)
2. Tell only someone you love or someone wise
3. Do not tell someone envious or ignorant

title_en: After a bad or frightening dream
paragraphs_en: 1. Blow lightly to your left three times
2. Seek refuge in Allah from Satan three times: A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim
3. Turn over onto your other side
4. If you wish, get up and pray
5. Tell no one; it will not harm you

title_en: Seeing the Prophet ﷺ in a dream
paragraphs_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot take my form.
Scholars say this applies when he is seen in the description given in the hadith.
Whoever describes a dream he did not see will be told on the Day of Judgement to tie a knot between two grains of barley, and he will never be able to do it.
The person most truthful in speech has the most truthful dreams.
Near the end of time, a believer's dream will hardly ever be false.

title_en: Whom to ask for an interpretation
paragraphs_en: Tell your dream only to a scholar or a well-wisher.
Abu Bakr (RA) interpreted a dream in front of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: you were right in some of it and wrong in some. So even the greatest interpreter gives an opinion, not knowledge of the unseen.
1. Sleep in a state of wudu
2. Lie on your right side and say the sleeping dua
3. Recite Ayat al-Kursi: protection from Allah through the night
4. Recite the three Quls, blow into your hands and wipe over your body
If you wake and find wetness on your clothes, ghusl is obligatory, whether or not you remember a dream. The same ruling applies to women.
Istikhara is a dua said after two rak'ahs of voluntary prayer.
Scholars say a dream is not required after istikhara; decide by your heart's inclination, advice and circumstances. Paying someone to 'do istikhara for you' is not from the Sunnah.
• No ruling of the Shariah is established by a dream; religion comes from the Quran and Sunnah.
• Not every dream has a meaning; many are just the self talking.
• Do not accuse a relative of black magic because of a dream.
• Avoid any 'baba' who claims to know your dream without being told, or promises a certain interpretation.
